δεήσει περὶ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων καὶ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ. ὁ ὑγιαίνων λόγο ἀπὸ θείου
πνεύματος ῥεῖ, ὁ δὲ ἐναντίο ἐκ τῆς γῆς λαλεῖ· ὁ γὰρ ὢν ἐκ τῆ γῆ ἐκ τῆ γῆ ἐ τι καὶ
ἐκ τῆ γῆ λαλεῖ· ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐρχό μενο ἐπάνω πάντων ἐ τίν· καὶ ὃ ἑώρακεν καὶ
ἤκου εν τοῦτο μαρτυρεῖ. ὁ δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος λόγος μάχαιρά ἐστιν, διόπερ ἐνταῦθά
φησιν ὁ Παῦλος τὴν μάχαιραν τοῦ πνεύματος εἶναι ῥῆμα Θεοῦ· ζῶν γὰρ ὁ λόγο τοῦ
Θεοῦ καὶ ἐνεργὴ καὶ τομώτερο ὑπὲρ πᾶ αν μάχαιραν δί τομον καὶ διικνούμενο ἄχρι
μερι μοῦ ψυχῆ καὶ πνεύματο τέμνει τε καὶ διαιρεῖ, ἀνύων καὶ διὰ τῆς προσευχῆς καὶ
δεησέως τοῖς ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ προσευχομένοις καὶ προσευχομένοις πνεύματι κατὰ τὸ
προ εύξομαι πνεύματι· καὶ ἀνύει τοῖς ὑπὲρ τοῦ πλουτῆσαι ἐν ῥήματι Θεοῦ
ἀγρυπνοῦσι, καὶ προσκαρτεροῦσι τῇ τούτου κτήσει, ἐπὶ τῷ καὶ ἄλλους ὠφελῆσαι καὶ
τοῖς ὠφελοῦσι διὰ τῶν εὐχῶν ἐνεργῆσαι. παρατήρει δὲ καὶ τὸ τοῦ ἀποστόλου
μέτριον, αἰτοῦντος ἀπὸ τῶν Ἐφεσίων δεήσεις γενέσθαι ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ. 36 Eph. vi19b
[ἵνα μοι δοθῇ λόγος ἐν ἀνοίξει τοῦ στόματός μου ἐν παρρησίᾳ γνωρίσαι τὸ
μυστήριον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου.] [Ὠριγένης] ὅταν ἀνοιχθῇ τὸ στόμα δοθέντος λόγου, τότε
παρρησίᾳ γνωρίζεται τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ οὐκέτι ἐν παροιμίαις καὶ
παραβολαῖς, ὡς καὶ ὁ σωτήρ φησιν ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὐκέτι ὑμῖν ἐν παροιμίαι
λαλή ω ἀλλὰ παρρη ίᾳ περὶ τοῦ πατρὸ ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν. τὸν δὲ ἐν παρρησίᾳ λόγον
μόνος καὶ πᾶς χωρῆσαι δύναται ὁ τὴν καρδίαν ἔχων μὴ καταγινώσκουσαν, ἐπεὶ ἐὰν
ἡ καρδία μὴ καταγινώ κῃ, παρρη ίαν ἔχομεν πρὸ τὸν Θεόν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτῶμεν
λαμβάνομεν παρ' αὐτοῦ. ὅθεν καὶ σπάνιος ὁ ἐν παρρησίᾳ γνωρίζων τὸ μυστήριον τῷ
σπάνιον εἶναι τὸν παρρη ίαν ἔχοντα πρὸ Θεόν. τί γὰρ καυχή εται ἁγνὴν ἔχειν τὴν
καρδίαν; ἢ τί παρρη ιά εται καθαρὸ εἶναι ἀπὸ ἁμαρτιῶν; [vi 21–22] ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε καὶ
ὑμεῖς τὰ κατ' ἐμέ, τί πράσσω, πάντα ὑμῖν γνωρίσει Τύχικος ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἀδελφὸς καὶ
πιστὸς διάκονος ἐν Κυρίῳ, ὃν ἔπεμψα πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἵνα γνῷ τὰ περὶ
ὑμῶν καὶ παρακαλέσῃ τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν. ἐπεὶ πᾶς ὁ τοῦ ἀποστόλου βίος καὶ πᾶσα
πρᾶξις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐνέργεια Λόγῳ Θεοῦ ἐγίνετο, ζῶντο ἐν αὐτῷ τοῦ Χρι τοῦ, διὰ
τοῦτο πέμπει τὸν Τύχικον, τὸν κανόνα τοῦ βίου καὶ τὴν τάξιν τῶν πράξεων αὐτοῦ
ἀπαγγελοῦντα τοῖς Ἐφεσίοις· καὶ ἔπρεπέ γε τῷ ἀποστόλῳ, ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔχειν
παράδειγμα πολιτείας ἀγαθῆς τοὺς Ἐφεσίους, πέμψαι δι' αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸν Τύχικον.
ἔμελλον δὲ καὶ παρακαλεῖσθαι, τὰ ἄριστα καὶ τὰ ἀποστόλῳ ἁρμόζοντα κατορθοῦσθαι
μανθάνοντες τῷ Παύλῳ. 37 Eph. vi23 [εἰρήνη τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καὶ ἀγάπη μετὰ πίστεως
ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.] [Ὠριγένης φησίν] εἰ καί τι ἄλλο δῶρόν
ἐστι διδόμενον ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ εἰρήνη·
ὅπερ ἓν τῶν τιμιωτάτων ἐστὶ δώρων, ἡ ὑπερέχου α πάντα νοῦν, ἥτις φρουρή ει τὰ
καρδία καὶ τὰ νοήματα τῶν ἁγίων, γαλήνη τις καὶ εὐδία οὖσα ψυχῆς, παντὸς
χειμῶνος καὶ πάσης ἀκαταστασίας καὶ πάθους ἀλλοτρία. ὁμοίως δὲ τῇ εἰρήνῃ καὶ ἡ
μετὰ πίστεως ἀγάπη δῶρόν ἐστι διδόμενον ἀπὸ Θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
ἀγάπη δὲ πρὸς Θεὸν μὲν ὡς γέγραπται ἐξ ὅλη καρδία καὶ τῶν ἑξῆς, πρὸς τὸν
πλη ίον δὲ ὡς ἑαυτόν· ἀλλὰ καὶ πρὸς τοὺ ἐχθροὺ ὁ λαβὼν δῶρον τὴν ἀγάπην
ἐπιφαίνει αὐτήν, οὐδένα μισῶν καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων εὐχόμενος. [vi 24] ἡ
χάρις μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἀγαπώντων τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ.
διηγήσαντό τινες εἶναι τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ, καθαρεύοντα ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων
τῆς φθορᾶς· ἔργα δὲ τῆς φθορᾶς ἐστι τὰ κατὰ τὴν συνουσίαν, ὅθεν καὶ ἡ συνήθεια
«ἀφθόρους» ὀνομάζει τοὺς καθαροὺς ἀπὸ συνουσίας, καὶ «ἐφθαρμένους» τοὺς
μίξεως γευσαμένους. ὑπερτείνοντες δέ τινες τὸ εἴ τι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φθείρει
φθερεῖ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεό οὕτως ἐδέξαντο· οὐ δυνάμενοι τούτῳ ὁμοίως σῶσαι τὸ ἀλλὰ
ἕκα το ἴδιον ἔχει χάρι μα ἐκ Θεοῦ, ὁ μὲν οὕτω , ὁ δὲ οὕτω . ὅρα δὲ εἰ δύναται πᾶσα
μὲν ἁμαρτία φθορὰ εἶναι ψυχῆς, ἡ δὲ παντελὴς αὐτῆς ἀποχὴ ἀφθαρσία· ὥστε τοὺς
ἀγαπῶντας τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ εἶναι τοὺς πάσης
ἁμαρτίας ἀπεχομένους· μεθ' ὧν πάντων ἐστὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ χάρις. ὡς ὄντων μέντοιγέ
τινων τῶν ἀγαπώντων μὲν τὸν Κύριον, οὐ μὴν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ ἀγαπώντων αὐτόν,
φησὶν ὁ Παῦλος ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἀγαπώντων τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν
Χριστὸν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: (... and) petition concerning all the saints and on behalf of me. The healthy word flows from the divine spirit, and the opposite speaks from the earth: for the one being from the earth is from the earth and speaks from the earth; the one coming from heaven is above all, and what he has seen and heard, this he testifies. And the word from the Spirit is a sword, which is why here Paul says the sword of the Spirit is the word of God; for living is the word of God and active and sharper beyond every two-edged sword and reaching through to the division of soul and spirit, it both cuts and divides, accomplishing also through prayer and petition for those praying in every season and praying with spirit according to 'I will pray with spirit'; and it accomplishes for those keeping vigil for the sake of becoming rich in the word of God, and persevering in the acquisition of it, with the aim both of benefiting others and of being at work, through the prayers, for those who benefit. And observe also the moderation of the apostle, asking from the Ephesians that petitions be made on his behalf. Eph 6:19b ['that word may be given me in the opening of my mouth, in boldness to make known the mystery of the gospel.'] [Origen:] when the mouth is opened, a word having been given, then in boldness the mystery of the gospel is made known and no longer in proverbs and parables, as also the Savior says 'an hour comes when no longer will I speak to you in proverbs but in boldness I will announce to you about the Father'. And the word in boldness only, and every, one having the heart not condemning can contain, since 'if the heart does not condemn, we have boldness toward God, and whatever we ask we receive from him'. Whence also rare is the one making known in boldness the mystery, by the having-boldness-toward-God one being rare. For who will boast to have a pure heart? Or who will speak boldly to be clean from sins? [6:21-22] 'and so that you also may know the things concerning me, what I do, Tychicus the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord will make all known to you, whom I sent to you for this very thing, that he may know the things about you and may comfort your hearts.' Since the whole life of the apostle and all his action and activity came about by the Word of God, Christ living in him, therefore he sends Tychicus, to announce to the Ephesians the rule of his life and the order of his actions; and it befitted the apostle, for the Ephesians to have an example of good citizenship, to send Tychicus for this very thing. And they were going also to be comforted, learning that the best things and things fitting for an apostle were being accomplished by Paul. Eph 6:23 ['peace to the brothers and love with faith from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.'] [Origen says:] if indeed also some other gift is given from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, also peace; which is one of the most honored gifts, the one surpassing every mind, which will guard the hearts and the thoughts of the saints, being a certain calm and fair-weather of soul, alien to every storm and every instability and passion. And likewise to peace the love with faith is also a gift given from God and the Lord Jesus Christ, love toward God as it is written 'from the whole heart' and what follows, and toward the neighbor 'as oneself'; but even toward the enemies the one who has received the gift of love displays it, hating no one and praying on behalf of those who abuse. [6:24] 'the grace with all those loving our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption.' Some have explained loving him in incorruption to be being pure from the works of corruption; and the works of corruption are those of sexual union, whence also custom names 'uncorrupted' those pure from union, and 'corrupted' those who have tasted mixing. And some, overstretching, received 'if anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him' thus; not being able likewise to save for this 'but each has his own gift from God, one thus, another thus'. And see whether every sin can be corruption of the soul, and the complete abstinence from it incorruption; so that those loving our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption are those abstaining from every sin; with all of whom is the grace of God. As however there being some of those loving the Lord, yet not loving him in incorruption, Paul says 'the grace with all those loving our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption'.
pass_b_english: petition for all the saints, and for me" (Ephesians 6:18-19). Sound speech flows from the divine Spirit, but its opposite speaks from the earth. For "the one who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks from the earth; the one who comes from heaven is above all, and what he has seen and heard, to that he bears witness" (John 3:31-32). The word that comes from the Spirit is a sword, and that is why Paul says here that the sword of the Spirit is the word of God. For "the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword," and "piercing to the division of soul and spirit" (Hebrews 4:12), it cuts and divides. It also does its work through prayer and petition for those who pray at every time, and who pray with the spirit, as in "I will pray with the spirit" (1 Corinthians 14:15). And it does its work for those who keep watch in order to grow rich in the word of God, and who persevere in acquiring it, so that they may both help others and, by their prayers, work on behalf of those who help them. Notice also the apostle's modesty: he asks the Ephesians to make petitions for him.

"So that speech may be given to me when I open my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel" (Ephesians 6:19). Origen: When the mouth is opened and speech has been given, then the mystery of the gospel is made known with boldness, and no longer in proverbs and parables. As the Savior too says, "The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but will tell you plainly about the Father" (John 16:25). Only the one whose heart does not condemn him can take in the word spoken with boldness, and everyone whose heart does not condemn him can. For "if our heart does not condemn us, we have boldness before God, and whatever we ask we receive from him" (1 John 3:21-22). So the one who makes the mystery known with boldness is rare, because the one who has boldness before God is rare. "For who will boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will speak boldly, claiming to be clean from sins?" (Proverbs 20:9).

"So that you also may know my affairs, how I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make everything known to you. I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that he may know how things are with you and may encourage your hearts" (Ephesians 6:21-22). Since the apostle's whole life, and every act and activity of his, came about by the Word of God, with Christ living in him, he sends Tychicus to report to the Ephesians the rule of his life and the order of his actions. And it was fitting for the apostle to send Tychicus for this very purpose, so that the Ephesians might have a pattern of good conduct. They were also going to be encouraged, as they learned that what was best, and what befits an apostle, was being achieved by Paul.

"Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" (Ephesians 6:23). Origen says: If there is any other gift given by God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, peace is one as well. It is one of the most precious gifts, "the peace that surpasses all understanding," which "will guard the hearts" and thoughts of the saints (Philippians 4:7). It is a kind of calm and fair weather of the soul, a stranger to every storm, all unrest, and passion. Like peace, love with faith is also a gift given by God and the Lord Jesus Christ: love toward God, as it is written, "with the whole heart" and the rest, and toward one's neighbor "as oneself" (Matthew 22:37-39). Indeed, the one who has received love as a gift shows it even toward his enemies, hating no one and praying for those who mistreat him (Luke 6:28).

"Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption" (Ephesians 6:24). Some have explained loving him in incorruption as being pure from the works of corruption, and the works of corruption are those of sexual union. That is why common usage calls those who are pure from intercourse "uncorrupted," and those who have tasted intercourse "corrupted." And some, stretching the point further, have taken "If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him" (1 Corinthians 3:17) in this way, though they cannot do the same justice to "But each has his own gift from God, one of one kind and one of another" (1 Corinthians 7:7). But see whether every sin may be a corruption of the soul, and complete abstinence from sin its incorruption. Then those who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption would be those who abstain from every sin, and the grace of God is with all of them. As though there were some who love the Lord, but do not love him in incorruption, Paul says, "Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption."

choices.english: that he may know how things are with you
choices.why: The Greek on disk reads γνῷ ... ὑμῶν (Tychicus learns about them); the old English printed the common text 'that you may know about us'.

choices.english: Only the one whose heart does not condemn him can take in ... and everyone whose heart does not condemn him can
choices.why: Keeps both 'only' and 'every' of μόνος καὶ πᾶς.

choices.english: though they cannot do the same justice to
choices.why: σῴζω here: keep a text consistent with one's reading; they cannot fit 1 Corinthians 7:7 to their reading.
